items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Designing catalytic materials with enhanced stability and activity is crucial for sustainable electrochemical energy technologies. RuO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    is the most active material for oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in electrolysers aiming at producing ‘green’ hydrogen, however it encounters critical electrochemical oxidation and dissolution issues during reaction. It remains a grand challenge to achieve stable and active RuO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    electrocatalyst as the current strategies usually enhance one of the two properties at the expense of the other. Here, we report breaking the stability and activity limits of RuO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    in neutral and alkaline environments by constructing a RuO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    /CoO
                    <jats:sub>
                      <jats:italic>x</jats:italic>
                    </jats:sub>
                    interface. We demonstrate that RuO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    can be greatly stabilized on the CoO
                    <jats:sub>
                      <jats:italic>x</jats:italic>
                    </jats:sub>
                    substrate to exceed the Pourbaix stability limit of bulk RuO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    . This is realized by the preferential oxidation of CoO
                    <jats:sub>
                      <jats:italic>x</jats:italic>
                    </jats:sub>
                    during OER and the electron gain of RuO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    through the interface. Besides, a highly active Ru/Co dual-atom site can be generated around the RuO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    /CoO
                    <jats:sub>
                      <jats:italic>x</jats:italic>
                    </jats:sub>
                    interface to synergistically adsorb the oxygen intermediates, leading to a favourable reaction path. The as-designed RuO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    /CoO
                    <jats:sub>
                      <jats:italic>x</jats:italic>
                    </jats:sub>
                    catalyst provides an avenue to achieve stable and active materials for sustainable electrochemical energy technologies.
                  </jats:p>
title: Interface engineering breaks both stability and activity limits of RuO2 for sustainable water oxidation

items.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>As the most promising alternative to platinum‐based catalysts for cathodic oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) in proton exchange membrane fuel cells, further performance enhancement of Fe–N–C catalysts is highly expected to promote their wide application. In Fe–N–C catalysts, the single Fe atom forms a square‐planar configuration with four adjacent N atoms (<jats:italic>D</jats:italic><jats:sub>4h</jats:sub> symmetry). Breaking the <jats:italic>D</jats:italic><jats:sub>4h</jats:sub> symmetry of the FeN<jats:sub>4</jats:sub> active center provides a new route to boost the activity of Fe–N–C catalysts. Herein, for the first time, the deformation of the square‐planar coordination of FeN<jats:sub>4</jats:sub> moiety achieved by introducing chalcogen oxygen groups (XO<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>, X = S, Se, Te) as polar functional groups in the Fe–N–C catalyst is reported. The theoretical and experimental results demonstrate that breaking the <jats:italic>D</jats:italic><jats:sub>4h</jats:sub> symmetry of FeN<jats:sub>4</jats:sub> results in the rearrangement of Fe 3<jats:italic>d</jats:italic> electrons and increases spin moment of Fe centers. The efficient spin state manipulation optimizes the adsorption energetics of ORR intermediates, thereby significantly promoting the intrinsic ORR activity of Fe–N–C catalysts, among which the SeO<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> modified catalyst lies around the peak of the ORR volcano plot. This work provides a new strategy to tune the local coordination and thus the electronic structure of single‐atom catalysts.</jats:p>
title: Tuning Fe Spin Moment in Fe–N–C Catalysts to Climb the Activity Volcano via a Local Geometric Distortion Strategy
